title: Japanese colonial empire (1895–1945)
summary: Japan’s overseas empire began when China ceded Taiwan (Formosa) under the Treaty of Shimonoseki of 17 April 1895. Japan annexed Korea in 1910, ruling it first through the military and crushing dissent, and in 1931 its army seized Manchuria and set up the puppet state of Manchukuo. In wartime from 1937 Koreans were forced into factories and military service, tens of thousands of women were taken as “comfort women”, and Koreans were pressed to take Japanese names. The empire ended with Japan’s surrender in 1945.

uncertainty.note: Begins with the signing of the Treaty of Shimonoseki ceding Taiwan on 17 April 1895; terminates with Japan's formal surrender in 1945.

importance.justification: Fifty years of colonial rule over Taiwan, Korea and Manchuria, with forced labour and wartime abuses (R3 D3 T2 L3).

audience_note: Covers colonial exploitation, forced labor, cultural assimilation policies, and wartime abuses across colonial Taiwan, Korea, and occupied territories.

related.because: Victory in the Russo-Japanese War consolidated Japanese dominance over Korea and southern Manchuria.
The military comfort women system drew extensively from colonized populations in Korea and Taiwan.
Colonial expansion culminated in full-scale invasion of mainland China from bases in Manchukuo and Taiwan.
Soviet entry crushed the Japanese Kwantung Army in Manchukuo, sealing the empire's collapse.
